newsitem.title: UK: World LPG falls despite lower CP and Karsto cutback.
newsitem.headline: World LPG falls despite lower CP and Karsto cutback.

text.p: International liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) markets continued their slide this week, with a cut in benchmark contract prices for Europe and the Far East failing to attract buyers into the market, traders said.
The Saudi contract price (CP), the key price marker for Gulf and Far East sales and an important market indicator for prices worldwide, was lowered for April for both propane and butane.
The propane contract price was cut by $72 to $198 per tonne and the price for butane fell by $70 to $207 per tonne.
But with prices still higher than year-ago levels, buyers were still keen to hold out for further cuts, traders said.
"Buyers say that the April CP is still too high, they're expecting an even lower CP for May," said one.
Dealers said that while stock levels of LPG in Asian markets were still very low, seasonally weak demand meant that buyers could afford to stick to the sidelines.
FOB Middle East Gulf premiums were notionally assessed at a discount of $20 a tonne to the CP, with freight rates to Japan and South Korea pegged at $18-$20 a tonne.
"Sellers want a premium to the CP (on a delivered basis) but buyers expect a reasonable discount," said a trader.
In Europe, a force majeure on sales from Norwegian's Statoil's Karsto terminal failed to boost prices.
A Statoil spokeswoman said on Friday that two days worth of production had been lost due to a crude supply hitch. Karsto produces 5,000 tonnes a day of propane and 2,500 tonnes a day of butane.
"There is a two-day delay in production, but it is not a big loss. Very few customers will notice," the spokeswoman said.
Indeed, the market shrugged off the news, with small propane cargoes trading at $185 and $181.50 fob NWE, with a larger cargo changing hands at $187 a tonne cif Sweden.
"If propane comes down any further I think we'll start seeing some buying from the petchem users," said one trader.
Small butane cargoes traded twice at $175 a tonne fob NWE on Thursday, with another deal heard done on a p+c basis below $170 on Friday.

Contract prices also fell, with the BP Agreed Price (BPAP) for April down $14 at $172 a tonne for propane and butane down $30 at $175 a tonne. Algeria's Sonatrach dropped its propane price by $20 to $175 a tonne and its butane price by $35 to $180 a tonne.
In the United States, propane prices at the Mont Belvieu trading hub in Texas fell by some $2.50 to $3 a tonne to around $35 a tonne.
